extensions.smallest_structural_change: Bind the client rules root to the repository rules path so only one writable tree remains. Two-tree drift is then not a possible state. A generator would also close the class, but [REDACTED] forbids a generated layer.
extensions.strongest_surviving_counterargument: A second live tree is how operators hot-patch a rule without waiting for a repo commit. Collapsing to one tree removes that operational valve. Detection-after-the-fact (Stop-hook warning) keeps the valve and still surfaces drift, which can be enough on a single-owner estate. That counterargument survives as an operational preference; it does not make two trees structurally consistent, and it does not restore the 2026-08-09 5/88 numbers on this Linux worktree where the live rules root is absent.
